extracted.intended_audience: academics/researchers who review for Cambridge University Press (and other Web of Science partner) journals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for Cambridge reviewers on how to record, claim, and manage recognition for peer reviews via the Web of Science Reviewer Recognition Service (formerly Publons). Covers claiming workflow, privacy/display controls, and benefits of having reviews added to a researcher profile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opt-in recognition when submitting to partner journals
rubrics_metrics.description: When you submit a review to a partner journal, you will be given the option to get recognition for your review on the Web of Science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you choose recognition you will be directed to create a Web of Science researcher profile to which your review is added. You can also elect to have all future reviews you complete for the journal automatically added to your profile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claiming reviews via private email link
rubrics_metrics.description: Once your review is completed you will receive an email with a private link to claim your review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the private link in the email to add the review to your researcher profile. The email-based private-link workflow is the mechanism for verification/claiming of individual reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workflow when reviewing for an integrated journal
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific steps for reviews on journals integrated with the Web of Science Reviewer Recognition Service: you will be asked if you want to get recognition; after completion you'll receive a private claim link; follow the link to add the review to your profile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integration implies a three-step interaction: opt-in prompt at submission, post-review claim email with private link, and adding the review to your researcher profile via that link.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy: reviewer anonymity preserved by default
rubrics_metrics.description: The Web of Science Reviewer Recognition Service gives recognition for peer review without compromising reviewer anonymity or infringing upon journal policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By default, the content of the review will not be publicly displayed; reviewer profiles will show only the year of the review and the journal title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control over displayed content and opt-out
rubrics_metrics.description: You may edit what is displayed for any review or opt out of the service at any time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users retain control of visibility for each claimed review (what appears on the profile) and can withdraw recognition if desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic addition of future reviews for a journal
rubrics_metrics.description: You can elect to have all future reviews you complete for the journal automatically added to your profile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This setting streamlines recognition for recurring reviewing on the same journal — it prevents needing to claim each review individually after opting in.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition applies even if reviews are anonymous or manuscript unpublished
rubrics_metrics.description: You get recognition even if your reviews are anonymous and the manuscript is never published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The service verifies and records the act of reviewing itself (year and journal) independent of publication outcome or public display of review text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefits: track, verify and showcase peer review activity for career purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: The Web of Science's researcher profile helps you to record, verify, and showcase your peer review contributions for use in promotion applications, performance evaluations and funding applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cambridge’s partnership provides a quick and easy way to link Cambridge reviews to your researcher profile so you receive recognition; the profile provides verifiable evidence of disciplinary expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal integration coverage (eligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: The majority of Cambridge's ScholarOne titles are integrated with the Web of Science Reviewer Recognition Service alongside a select number of journals using Editorial Manager.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether a given review is claimable depends on the journal's integration status; reviewers should check if the journal uses ScholarOne or is listed as integrated.
